brief: “Jesus” is a version of the Hebrew name Yeshua (Joshua), very common among Jews in antiquity. In the gospel story, the weight falls not on Jesus’ circumcision (the sign of the covenant) but on his naming. The name was thought to mean “The Lord saves”; Jesus is to “save his people from their sins”. The name “Jesus” occurs frequently in the New Testament, often, outside the Gospels, in combinations like “the Lord Jesus”, “Christ Jesus”, or “Jesus Christ”.
